scope: Applicability and identified controls; not a new architecture, trained model, or verified CVPR contribution

variables.S: Actual exposed native object state, registry/config where available
variables.U: Original user requirements, retaining ambiguity and unsupported clauses
variables.A: A proposed executable action with exact identities and arguments
variables.Y: Measured post-action geometry or a supported check vector
variables.mu: Archived behavior policy, not an expert by default
variables.H: A proposed desired geometric/relational subgoal, not a measured future

claims.name: Known transition is not a novel world model
claims.formula: For fixed supported deterministic T and checker F, Y=F(T(S,A),U). Given S,A,T,F, H(Y|S,A)=0 for discrete Y.
assumptions: No unobserved stage, model output or physical interaction
not_implied: A neural policy can choose a good A
Representation learning cannot help finite models
claims.evidence: Previously published ordinary-control 823/823 comparisons, reused without new predictor calls; native source contracts separately read

claims.name: Descriptive future and desired future differ
claims.formula: p_mu(Y|S,U)=sum_A p(Y|S,U,A) mu(A|S,U). Training to this mixture does not identify an optimal-task future distribution.
assumptions: Observed actions belong to the logged behavior distribution
not_implied: Bad outcomes cannot train an action-conditioned dynamics/negative-outcome model
Multi-modal future prediction is inherently invalid
MSE ambiguity proves CPR or GeomVLA fails
claims.evidence: New 72-row role audit, 25/35 native moves with recorded damage, no independent desired-future labels

claims.name: Prediction loss can average behavior, not solve the task
claims.formula: For squared error and fixed target coordinates, argmin_g E||Y-g(X)||^2=E[Y|X]; conditional variance is the irreducible risk for that X. SmoothL1 has a different estimating equation, not generally this mean.
assumptions: This is a mathematical population statement for a fixed X and fixed target, not an estimate of model generalization
not_implied: The extracted state/task X contains full model history
The empirical table is a learned model
Zero in-sample X,A risk identifies deterministic population dynamics
A target mean must correspond to a feasible scene or useful action
A flexible latent representation cannot avoid this fixed-coordinate loss geometry
claims.evidence: 10/41 state-task groups have different measured check vectors; native-move-only restriction still has 2/25 groups

claims.name: Information and computation are separate
claims.formula: A deterministic feature of available X has zero conditional information I(A;f(X)|X), but may change approximation, optimization or computation of a bounded model.
assumptions: Same actual X and deterministic feature, no hidden labels supplied
not_implied: An auxiliary geometry feature is useless
Any improvement is automatically a new method
claims.control: Compare explicit native-state/ordinary-lookahead inputs, pose auxiliary supervision and equal-budget direct-action search before attributing benefit to predictive geometry.

target_roles.data: Original audited current object geometry/available views
target_roles.known_gap: Views missing on 5/24 original units; no replacement view fabrication

target_roles.meaning: Descriptive transition or negative outcome, not desired arrangement
target_roles.known_gap: 72 rows remain evaluation-only; ordinary control covers supported checks; no independent room/operator coverage

target_roles.role: desired goal H conditioned on S,U
target_roles.data: Must be anchored to original requirements and verified candidates or independent demonstrations
target_roles.known_gap: No such independently established labels added by this audit; do not copy all behavior futures

target_roles.data: Native complete-room outcomes plus full-task assessment
target_roles.known_gap: Local changes, name binding and unknown checks cannot be promoted to whole-room success

next_algorithm_comparison.primary: Original same-source action-only, D-auxiliary direct-action, and self-generated D-conditioned action comparison remains the identified supervised question; geometric future prediction is a control, not a replacement claim.
complete_generation_contract: Begin from the original text and common native backend; preserve required instance identities and all unmet/unknown clauses.
Let all policies query the same actual state and use the same asset, add, move, remove and supported relation operations.
For known transition/checks, use the same ordinary preview in all compared arms rather than call one arm a world model.
If testing H, explicitly tag it as desired subgoal. Shared original H labels must also train an auxiliary-H direct-action control; no teacher H/future observations at deployment.
Decode the action, execute on a candidate copy, obtain actual results and continue from that actual state. Do not use frozen teacher trajectories as end-to-end policy execution.
Score full original requirements, semantic unknowns, instance completeness, geometric/function limits, collateral edits and all model/tool/render costs.
required_controls: Direct action + common native state/ordinary endpoint check/search
Direct action + original D auxiliary labels (same data as D-conditioned arm)
Self-generated D -> action (no supplied teacher D at inference)
If geometry is introduced: same geometry labels as ordinary auxiliary head with direct action
If future-goal H is introduced: H auxiliary vs H-conditioned action with identical valid labels, model budget and candidate operations
next_algorithm_comparison.novelty_boundary: HSM/SceneSmith already combine generation, structured state and feedback; NaLA has explicit layout geometry. D conditioning, future auxiliary prediction, ordinary search and rollback are not independently new contributions.
next_algorithm_comparison.escalation_rule: No new large teacher/robot data download. First show a full-room, held-out benefit beyond ordinary state/geometry/auxiliary controls, or revise the mechanism. This audit provides no such benefit yet.
